overview: Tenacity 5.1's Disabler is a setting-driven anticheat bypass module built around a single MultipleBoolSetting named 'Disablers' that holds 13 named toggles. Every handler iterates that setting group, filters enabled toggles, and switches on the toggle name, so behavior is driven entirely by which names are active. Three Module overrides carry the logic: onMotionEvent for tick-based buffer flushing and input spam, onPacketSendEvent for cancelling, rewriting and buffering serverbound packets, and onPacketReceiveEvent for suppressing server teleports. The modes split into Hypixel-targeted Watchdog bypasses, the MMC and Omni Sprint sprint-state desyncs, and a row of generic packet transforms that cancel, rewrite or replay C03, C0B, C0C, C0F, C00 and S08 packets.

sections.p: Disabler is a name-based state machine. All 13 bypasses live as BooleanSettings inside one MultipleBoolSetting, and each event handler iterates the group, checks isEnabled, and switches on the setting name string. Three Module overrides drive everything: onMotionEvent runs every client tick (MMC buffer flush, Watchdog Timer spike, C0C input spam), onPacketSendEvent intercepts every serverbound packet and holds the bulk of the logic, and onPacketReceiveEvent handles inbound traffic for the Silent S08 mode. Packet storage uses CopyOnWriteArrayList buffers because packets are added on the send path and flushed from the tick handler. The constructor wires the three tuning values (TPDelay, hoverHeight, onGround) to their parent toggles with addParent so they only render in the UI when the matching mode is enabled.

The modes reduce to three primitives. Inline mutation edits the packet before it hits the wire: Hover replaces the y of every position-carrying C03 with the player's real posY plus hoverHeight, Spoof Ground forces the onGround flag to the On Ground setting, and Void TP subtracts 1000 from the packet y every TPDelay ticks. Type rewriting swaps the packet object inside the event: C06->C04 rebuilds a position-look as a plain C04 position, dropping yaw and pitch, while C04->C06 attaches the client's current rotationYaw and rotationPitch to a plain position. Cancel-and-replay parks cancelled packets in a buffer and releases them later through PacketUtils.sendPacketNoEvent, which sends straight through the network manager with the silent flag so a replay never re-enters the PacketSendEvent hook that cancelled it in the first place.

The Hypixel modes are gated by ServerUtils.isOnHypixel, which requires the server IP to contain 'hypixel' and the client brand to start with 'Hypixel BungeeCord'. Watchdog Strafe only acts while the Speed module is enabled and fallDistance is under 1: it forces onGround true, then cancels and buffers every C03 except on ticks where ticksExisted is a multiple of 4, where the whole buffer flushes at once, so the server sees movement in bursts instead of a steady stream. Watchdog Timer cancels stationary C03s outright (those with neither the moving nor the rotating flag set) and parks C0F transactions and C00 keepalives inside a 350ms window, flushing the backlog when the window elapses, while a 700ms spike timer keeps restarting that window. MMC and Omni Sprint cancel every C0B entity action, and when a START_SPRINTING arrives while EntityPlayerSP.serverSprintState says the server still believes the player is sprinting, they inject a STOP_SPRINTING first and clear the flag, so the server permanently tracks the player as not sprinting while the client sprints freely. Silent S08 cancels the server teleport and re-sends its position as a C06 with onGround=false, confirming the coordinates without the client-side snap. Verus and C0B Cancel are blanket cancels of C0F/C00 and C0B respectively, and C0C Spam pushes a fresh zeroed C0CPacketInput every tick.

files.label: Disabler.java
files.explanation:
The module's entire behavior is selected by the 13 BooleanSettings inside the 'Disablers' MultipleBoolSetting; the settings carry no logic, they are dispatch keys. onMotionEvent, onPacketSendEvent and onPacketReceiveEvent each iterate disablers.getBoolSettings(), skip disabled toggles, and switch on booleanSetting.name, so renaming a toggle silently changes what the module does. The three tuning values (TPDelay, hoverHeight, onGround) are bound to their modes in the constructor with addParent, and the module suffix reflects how many toggles are enabled.

onMotionEvent runs once per client tick. The MMC case flushes the packets buffer every 1000-1500ms via MathUtils.getRandomInRange with timer reset, so the replay cadence is randomized rather than fixed. The Watchdog Timer case resets the 350ms window timer every 700ms through spikeTimer, so the desync window keeps restarting. The C0C Spam case sends a fresh default C0CPacketInput through sendPacketNoEvent every tick; all four of its fields (strafeSpeed, forwardSpeed, jumping, sneaking) default to zero, which the server's processInput applies to the player's entity action state.

onPacketSendEvent holds most of the logic. Watchdog Strafe, gated by ServerUtils.isOnHypixel, only acts while the Speed module is enabled and fallDistance is under 1: it forces the C03 onGround flag true, then cancels and buffers every C03 except on ticks where ticksExisted is a multiple of 4, at which point the backlog flushes in a burst, staggering the movement stream Watchdog samples. Watchdog Timer cancels C03s that are neither moving (the flag C04 and C06 set) nor rotating, and while the 350ms window has not elapsed it cancels and parks every C0F transaction and C00 keepalive, flushing them when the window elapses. MMC cancels every C0B: a START_SPRINTING is preceded by an injected STOP_SPRINTING whenever EntityPlayerSP.serverSprintState is true, and the flag is cleared, so the server's sprint state can never turn on; MMC also parks C0F and C00 packets in the packets buffer for the tick handler to flush. The generic transforms then rewrite or mutate C03 traffic: C06->C04 rebuilds position-look packets as plain positions, C04->C06 reattaches the current rotation, Hover raises the packet y by hoverHeight, Spoof Ground overwrites the onGround flag, Void TP subtracts 1000 from y every TPDelay ticks, and C0B Cancel and Verus blanket-cancel C0B or C0F/C00 packets with no replay.

onPacketReceiveEvent handles one mode: Silent S08 cancels an incoming S08PacketPlayerPosLook and immediately re-sends the teleport coordinates as a C06 with onGround=false via sendPacketNoEvent, so the server's correction is confirmed without the client ever snapping to it. onWorldEvent clears the Watchdog Timer buffer and resets the timer on world change. The file also carries dead weight: isBlockUnder(), a downward collision scan over 2-block steps, is never called, and joinTimer, synced, watchdogInvPackets, s08Y, spiking and airTicks are declared but never used, leftovers from earlier iterations.

files.label: PacketUtils.java
files.explanation:
PacketUtils is the send primitive every Disabler replay depends on. sendPacketNoEvent(Packet) calls sendPacket(packet, true), which routes through mc.getNetHandler().getNetworkManager().sendPacket(packet, silent). The silent boolean is the key: Tenacity's network layer fires PacketSendEvent for non-silent sends, so a silent send reaches the server without being offered back to the module's onPacketSendEvent handler. That is what makes the cancel-and-replay modes work: a packet cancelled from the event stream can be parked, then re-sent later without being cancelled or rewritten a second time.

The class is shared across the client. The non-silent overload sendPacket(Packet) goes through the event bus normally, and isPacketValid filters out handshake, login, status and ping packets that are not play-phase traffic. In Disabler all three flush paths (watchdogPlayerPackets, watchdogC0FC00Packets and packets) call sendPacketNoEvent, so every replay bypasses the module's own interception.

files.label: ServerUtils.java
files.explanation:
ServerUtils.isOnHypixel() gates both Watchdog modes. It first rejects singleplayer and missing ServerData, then requires the server IP string to contain 'hypixel'. Once the player entity exists it goes further: the server's brand, read from getClientBrand and populated by the server's plugin channel, must start with 'Hypixel BungeeCord'. The check therefore rules out lookalike servers that merely have 'hypixel' in their address, so the Watchdog bypasses only engage against a genuine Hypixel proxy.

The class also holds helpers the rest of the client uses elsewhere: serverCheck matches an IP suffix, isGeniuneHypixel combines the brand check with a hosts-file redirect flag, and isInLobby scans loaded entities for Hypixel's CLICK TO PLAY NPC. None of those are used by Disabler, which only ever calls isOnHypixel.

countering.label: KeepAliveFrequency (keepalive rate)
countering.explanation:
KeepAliveAdapter (NCPCompatProtocolLib/src/main/java/fr/neatmonster/nocheatplus/checks/net/protocollib/KeepAliveAdapter.java) registers at ListenerPriority.LOW for Play.Client.KEEP_ALIVE and Play.Server.KEEP_ALIVE. Every inbound C00 is first fed to recordKeepAlivePacketDetails, which calls NetData.recordKeepAlivePacket to track the packet id, the previous id, a duplicate flag, and whether the reply matches an outstanding server request (keepAliveExpectedResponse), then frequencyCheck.check runs. Each C00 adds 1f to data.keepAliveFreq, an ActionFrequency(20, 1000): twenty 1-second buckets covering 20 seconds. The check triggers on bucketScore(0) > 1f, i.e. more than one keepalive in the current second, and sizes the violation as max(first - limit, fullScore - numberOfBuckets), where the first-bucket limit is 2f normally, 1f for duplicate ids, or a 3-6f fallback when the server's outgoing keepalives are not tracked.

This is a direct counter to Watchdog Timer. That mode cancels every C00 keepalive and C0F transaction, parks them in a CopyOnWriteArrayList, and flushes the entire backlog when the 350ms window elapses, while a 700ms spike timer keeps restarting the window. The flush is a burst: several C00s land inside the same 1-second bucket. The check already tolerates one reply per outstanding server request (check returns false when keepAliveExpectedResponse && !keepAliveDuplicateId), so a single buffered reply passes; the second and third replies in the same second are unexpected - the server had no outstanding request for them - and drive bucketScore(0) above 1f. isModeledBoundaryBurst only exempts a single adjacent pair whose ids are strictly increasing (the monotonic check against keepAlivePacketId/keepAlivePreviousPacketId) while the 20-second fullScore stays under numberOfBuckets + 2f; a repeating 350ms flush cadence accumulates fullScore past that threshold and the exemption dies. Actions are 'cancel vl>10 cancel log:keepalive:2:6:i vl>60 cancel log:keepalive:0:10:icf cmdc:kickalive:0:5' (DefaultConfig NET_KEEPALIVEFREQUENCY_ACTIONS): cancel at vl>10, kick at vl>60, and keepAliveFrequencyStartupDelay exempts the first moments after join.

Bypass surface: only the keepalive half of Watchdog Timer's C00/C0F pair is scored - NCP has no transaction-frequency check, so the C0F side is invisible here. If the server's keepalive interval is long relative to the 350ms flush, each flush can carry exactly one reply and the expected-response exemption swallows it; the technique only accrues vl when flushes repeatedly stack two or more replies into one second. The id-monotonicity exemption also forgives an occasional 2-packet burst as a netty/Folia timestamp artifact.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation:
MovingListener.checkPlayerMove invokes morePackets.check on every serverbound move (MovingListener line 1561). data.morePacketsFreq is an ActionFrequency(morePacketsEPSBuckets, 500): 500ms buckets across a 6-second window, and NetStatic.morePacketsCheck scores it against three criteria with DefaultConfig values: EPS accumulation (morePacketsEPSMax 22/s vs morePacketsEPSIdeal 20/s), a direct burst (bucketScore(0) > morePacketsBurstPackets 15 packets within half a second, tagged 'burstdirect', capped by morePacketsBurstDirect 10 events, i.e. 150 packets per 500ms), and burst events per minute (morePacketsBurstEPM 95, tagged 'burstepm'). Excess in the newest bucket is first redistributed into later empty buckets, idle windows are burnt at the ideal rate, and only server lag measured by TickTask is counted as free allowance. On violation the player is set back to the pre-flush location (getMorePacketsSetBack); actions are 'cancel vl>2 cancel log:morepackets:10:9:i vl>100 cancel log:morepackets:0:2:ifc cmdc:kickpackets:0:10', cancelling at vl>2.

Against Tenacity this check catches any configuration that actually inflates C03 throughput above the envelope. Watchdog Strafe is the interesting case: it is a queue-and-replay that preserves the aggregate rate - it cancels 3 of 4 C03s and flushes the backlog on ticks where ticksExisted is a multiple of 4, so 20 packets/s still leave the client and each flush is only about 4 packets, below the 15-per-500ms burst threshold. At default config the steady state is therefore not flagged; the check bites when module traffic stacks on top of the move stream - a Silent S08 confirming C06 re-sent while the player keeps moving, or a Watchdog Timer flush landing in the same window as normal moves - pushing a 500ms bucket over 15 or building burstepm over a minute.

Bypass surface: C0C Spam is invisible here - C0CPacketInput never reaches the move listener, so 20 zeroed input packets per tick do not touch morePacketsFreq, and the C0F/C00 backlog is equally invisible. The 22/s EPS cap leaves roughly 10% headroom that a disabler can consume by replaying one extra move per second.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (movement envelope)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly.check compares every serverbound move against a physics envelope. LostGround.runLostGroundChecks runs first (line 146), correlating the client's onGround flag with server-side ground state. Horizontal allowance comes from prepareSpeedEstimation, vertical allowance from vDistRel, which derives yAllowedDistance from the previous move's y-distance and the from/to ground conditions (fromOnGround/toOnGround via isOnGroundOpportune block-change tracking). The violation amount is (max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0)) * 100D, then handleViolation. Critically, the sprint multiplier is applied to the allowed horizontal acceleration only when pData.isSprinting() is true (lines 739-741: 'acceleration += acceleration * 0.3f'), and that flag mirrors the server-side sprint state, set from Bukkit's PlayerToggleSprintEvent (CombinedListener.onToggleSprint calls setSprintingState), which fires from the server's C0B-driven sprint handling.

This one check counters four of the module's modes. Void TP subtracts 1000 from the packet y every TPDelay ticks: a single move with yDistance around 1000 against a yAllowedDistance bounded by terminal velocity produces an unbounded violation. Spoof Ground and Watchdog Strafe force onGround=true on every rewritten C03; while the player is genuinely airborne (falls, ledge strafes) LostGround's flag-vs-physics correlation flags the mismatch. MMC and Omni Sprint desync the server-side sprint state by cancelling every C0B and injecting STOP_SPRINTING, so the server (and NCP's tracked flag) believes the player is walking - which is exactly what the envelope is keyed to: the client's real sprint-speed movement exceeds the walk-speed allowance. Hover's constant hoverHeight bias cancels in the per-move delta on flat ground but pushes yDistance past yAllowedDistance on stairs, slabs and uneven terrain.

Bypass surface: flat-ground hover with a small hoverHeight, the burst timing of Watchdog Strafe (each replayed step is an individually valid queued position), and the Silent S08 confirming C06 (teleport-confirming moves are the one case NCP expects to be large). The sprint desync only pays off on servers that do not key allowed speed to the server-side sprint state - which is precisely why those modes target MMC and Omni rather than NCP-protected servers.

countering.label: Flight (vertical motion)
countering.explanation:
Arc's MovingListener recomputes per-move vertical = abs(distanceVertical(from, to)) and derives server-side ground from LocationHelper.isOnGround(to, vertical): a solid-block probe 0.5 below the reported position with a 0.3-step horizontal expansion, tracked in MovingData separately from the client's own onGround flags (flyingClientOnGround/positionClientOnGround, set from the FLYING/POSITION/POSITION_LOOK wrappers in PacketListener). Flight.check then runs the hover, vertical-clip, ascension, glide and Jesus stages. Any vertical move of 0.99 or more (vertical >= 0.99) enters the Vertical Clip loop, which walks every block between the safe location and the target and flags 'vclip_solid' if any is solid.

Void TP's -1000 y rewrite is a vertical of 1000, so the clip loop scans the whole span, finds solid ground along it and flags immediately. Spoof Ground's forced onGround=true trips the Jesus stage in liquids: in water, ccGround (the client flag) true while vertical > 0.0 flags 'walking on water' - Arc's own onGround is server-computed, so the spoofed flag only feeds specific staged checks. Hover trips the hover stage when the reported position is genuinely unsupported: the 0.5-block probe still reads small biases over flat ground as supported, but over ledges, gaps or with larger offsets the player reads as airborne with zero vertical speed, and airTicks >= max-hover-time flags 'hovering off the ground'. The Silent S08 confirming C06 gets no exemption - Arc registers no server teleport tracking at all, its listener set covers only client movement wrappers - so a long horizontal confirm move is cancelled by Speed's hard cap (Speed.check: 'if (thisMove > 8) return true;') and a long vertical one by the clip loop.

Bypass surface: C0C Spam is invisible - only position-carrying wrappers increment flyingPackets/positionPackets, and Vrekt MorePackets resets and checks those counters once per second with max-packets 30. Watchdog Strafe's burst replay is timing-invisible: each of the 4 replayed moves is a legal step and per-move checks see 4 ordinary moves. The sprint desync also passes Arc's Speed on flat ground, because the base allowance of 0.2873 blocks per tick already covers sprint speed - the desync is only countered by NCP's sprint-keyed envelope, not by Arc.
